title: Street Level: New York Photographs 1987-2007

description.main: Twenty years of black-and-white New York photographs by Sue Kwon, from hip-hop portraits to street scenes, with an introduction by Hilton Als.
description.extended:
Twenty years of black-and-white New York photographs by Sue Kwon, ranging from hip-hop portraits to street scenes in the city's neighborhoods.

Street Level collects documentary and commercial work made between 1987 and 2007, with an introduction by Hilton Als. Its subjects include the Beastie Boys, Biggie Smalls and the Wu-Tang Clan, and scenes from Little Italy, Chinatown, Coney Island, the Lower East Side and Times Square before Giuliani. Shoe-shiners, inmates at Rahway State Prison, newlyweds and strippers between sets at Sue's Rendezvous appear as well. The publisher compares the pictures to Helen Levitt's and calls this the first complete monograph of Kwon's work.

Kwon began at the Village Voice, photographing subjects from N.W.A. to Covenant House runaways to underground Jamaican nightclubs in Queens. She then shot mostly hip-hop artists for labels including Def Jam, Sony and Loud Records, and lives and works in New York.
